ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors and senior managers against Gibraltar, HM Treasury, UN, EU and OFAC sanctions lists; mandatory PEP identification and enhanced due diligence; adverse-media checks and source-of-wealth evidence required before incorporation; annual re-certification and ongoing transaction monitoring are imposed by the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry (GFSC online submission and e-Registry portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Roman/Latin script; foreign-script names must be transliterated into English; diacritical marks outside standard Latin characters are not accepted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may request a written statement of grounds, submit an administrative appeal to the Registrar within 14 calendar days, and thereafter apply to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar for judicial review; a new name may be tendered without prejudice and a pre-expiry extension of reservation can be applied to the Registry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not accepted for an AML-proscribed payroll SaaS operation; Gibraltar requires a physical registered office in the jurisdiction, with local corporate secretary and substantive employment records at the disposal of the GFSC.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 62% quantified risk of an unannounced inspection in the first fiscal year; >80% once any payment-institution license or EMI registration is triggered.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, sections 6(1)–6(3), 17, 24, 31 and 33; Income Tax Act 2010 (as amended), Part 12 (exempt companies).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Gibraltar Registry of Companies (Registrar of Companies), HM Government of Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 2 – Application for Incorporation, together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Gibraltar private exempted company limited by shares, and no escrow or capital deposit is required; the subscriber shares are declared in the Statement of Capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the subscribers be and are hereby allotted the initial ordinary shares at par, credited as fully paid; (2) that the registered office be fixed at [address] in Gibraltar and the Registrar of Companies notified accordingly; (3) that [Name] and [Name] be appointed as first Directors and [Name] as Company Secretary, each holding office under the Articles; (4) that a company bank account be opened at [bank] and the Directors be authorised to execute account documentation; (5) that this resolution be entered in the Company's minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Registered Office Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Registry of Companies (online Companies House e-Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application via the Gibraltar Companies House e-Registry and check name availability. Ensure the proposed name does not imply a regulated activity (e.g., banking, insurance, investment services). Confirm the registered office address in Gibraltar, to be provided by a licensed corporate service provider or local agent.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address (lease or service agreement)
Passport copies of the initial directors/subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, choose an alternative name and re-file, or submit a written representation to the Registrar under section 7(3) of the Companies Act 2014.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarisation of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public and the subscribers' legal advisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in accordance with the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 model articles. The document must provide for a single class of ordinary shares, appoint at least one director and one company secretary, and include a registered office clause. Each subscriber must sign the Memorandum in the presence of a notary public.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed and notarised)
Consent forms of the first directors and secretary
Statement of capital and initial shareholdings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the constitutional documents (e.g., ambiguous objects clause), amend and re-submit with a cover letter and a new Form ARCS; no additional state fee is charged for a resubmission within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with the Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete incorporation application online or in person at the Registry, attaching the notarised Memorandum and Articles, the statement of compliance, and the prescribed fee. The application must be signed by a subscriber or by a licensed corporate service provider. The Registrar will issue a certificate of incorporation upon satisfactory review.
required_dossiers: Notarised Memorandum and Articles of Association
Receipt for payment of the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or placed under query, correct the stated defects and file an amended application within 21 calendar days; a late response may incur a late-filing penalty of GIP 50.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of Directors and Company Secretary (First Board Meeting)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors (convened by the initial subscribers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a first board meeting or pass a written resolution within 14 days of incorporation. Approve the issue of shares to the subscribers, adopt the registered office as fixed in the constitutional documents, appoint the first directors and company secretary, and authorise the opening of a corporate bank account. Record all actions in the company's statutory books.
required_dossiers: Minutes or written resolution of the first board meeting
Consent to act forms from the directors and secretary
Share certificates issued to the subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a consent form is missing or defective, the company may file a statutory declaration of regularity and request the Registrar to accept the late filing without penalty, provided the omission is corrected within 28 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Status Election and Data Protection Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Commissioner of Income Tax; Gibraltar Information Commissioner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the statutory window (generally 9 months from incorporation), submit an election for exempt/non-resident tax status under the Income Tax Act to obtain the Tax Exempt Zone classification. Separately, register as a data controller with the Gibraltar Information Commissioner because the company will process payroll and HR personal data. Retain the registered office certificate and corporate documents for the application.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and registered office certificate
Identity documents of all directors and the company secretary
Data protection registration form (DPR-1) and processing description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax election is refused, file an appeal with the Tax Appeal Commission within 30 days; for data protection, amend the registration to add any additional processing categories or security measures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – pure digital service provider (ISIC 6201) with no industrial or manufacturing premises; if physical premises are later established, the relevant authority is the Gibraltar Industrial Licensing Board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no manufacturing, operative, or trade-specific licence is required for a payroll automation software platform operating as a non-resident exempt company.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Gibraltar Environment Agency (Department of Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the business generates no physical emissions, wastewater, or waste streams. No EIA registration or report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. In the event the company later installs server hardware in Gibraltar, it will become subject to the Control of Pollution Act and the Waste Management Act 2017 for any electronic waste and standby power emissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a software-only business with no physical office footprint in Gibraltar. If a local office is subsequently opened, the company must obtain a fire safety clearance and a workplace inspection certificate under the Health and Safety at Work Act (Gibraltar).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office, Ministry of Finance, HM Government of Gibraltar, 143-149 Town Range, Gibraltar GX11 1AA; official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/income-tax (entity e-filing via the Income Tax Office online returns system); corporate registration portal: Companies House Gibraltar, https://www.csra.gi. HMRC (UK) is not the competent authority for Gibraltar local taxation; Gibraltar is a separate tax jurisdiction outside the UK VAT and direct tax systems.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Bermuda Exempted Company with Companies House Gibraltar as an overseas company under the Companies Act 2014, filing certified certificate of incorporation, memorandum/articles, board resolution, registered office address and local process agent details. Step 2: Submit the Income Tax Office company registration form, beneficial ownership declaration, Gibraltar registered business address and constitutional documents; the Commissioner will issue a Gibraltar Tax Identification Number (TIN) for the foreign entity. Step 3: File the annual corporate tax return on territorial profits; if central management and control remains outside Gibraltar, a non-resident declaration should be filed to avoid Gibraltar tax residency while retaining the Gibraltar TIN. Step 4: Maintain Bermuda exempted status through annual declarations to the Bermuda Registrar of Companies via the registered resident representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — the Bermuda Exempted Company is tax-exempt in Bermuda (no Bermuda income tax, capital gains tax or withholding tax) but, when registered to carry on business in Gibraltar, becomes chargeable to Gibraltar corporation tax at 12.5% only on profits accruing in or derived from Gibraltar (territorial attribution). If central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar, the company is treated as a Gibraltar tax resident under section 82 of the Income Tax Act 2010, with the same territorial charge; foreign-source profits remain outside the Gibraltar tax base.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or entity classification election exists in Gibraltar; residence is determined factually by central management and control. The former Qualifying Company (Category 2) regime is closed to new entrants (phased out by 2010). Hybrid mismatch rules (Taxes (Hybrid Mismatch) Regulations 2017, aligned with OECD BEPS Action 2) apply without elective carve-outs; no statutory election is available to treat the Bermuda Exempted Company as pass-through or disregarded for Gibraltar tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST/Sales-and-Use-Tax in Gibraltar; Gibraltar is outside the UK VAT area and indirect taxation is limited to customs import duties and excise on a narrow list of physical goods. Software-as-a-service (ISIC 6201) exports and payroll automation subscription revenues are outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax; UK VAT (20%) may apply to UK customers under reverse-charge or overseas supplier registration rules, but that is an HMRC regime, not a Gibraltar charge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no registration threshold exists because Gibraltar does not levy VAT/GST on services; import duty is generally zero-rated on entry of goods into Gibraltar, with excise only on alcohol, tobacco and fuel.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Not applicable — Gibraltar has no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory e-invoicing/API requirement, no digital stamping regime and no clearance portal for invoices; standard electronic or paper invoicing with a complete audit trail is sufficient for Gibraltar tax compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — Gibraltar has no VAT/GST zero-rating mechanism; cross-border SaaS and payroll-automation services invoiced from Gibraltar are outside the scope of any Gibraltar indirect tax, so no zero-rating claim or export refund procedure is required. If the company voluntarily registers for UK VAT to supply UK customers, UK zero-rating for exported services may apply under VATA 1994, but that is administratively outside Gibraltar's regime.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: N/A — no Gibraltar Customs Export Declaration applies to intangible SaaS services because no physical movement of goods occurs.
N/A — no Bill of Lading or airway bill exists for electronically supplied services; retain the executed MSA, SaaS subscription order, service delivery logs and IP right evidence instead.

Inward remittance evidence (SWIFT MT103, bank credit advice or statement) should be retained for territorial profit-attribution and transfer-pricing audits; no statutory FX repatriation certificate is mandatory in Gibraltar.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Gibraltar has no VAT zero-rating regime, so no indirect-tax clawback is applicable. However, misstatement of territorial profits in Gibraltar corporate tax returns attracts penalties under the Income Tax Act 2010 (as amended): up to 100% of the tax underpaid for negligence and up to 150% for fraudulent or wilful default, plus daily default penalties, interest and potential criminal prosecution. If the company voluntarily registers for UK VAT and makes a false zero-rating claim, UK Finance Act 2007 Schedule 24 penalties (up to 100% of lost revenue) and interest would apply. Gibraltar has no statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is a documentary and transfer-pricing convention for export proceeds realization in cross-border SaaS operations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC). Gibraltar has no central bank; the Government of Gibraltar issues Gibraltar pound (GIP) notes, legal tender only in Gibraltar, fully backed at par by pound sterling reserves held with the Bank of England. The GFSC regulates banking, anti-money laundering, and payment services under the Financial Services Act 2019 and the AML Act 2019. The Bermuda Exempted Company is supervised at entity level by the Bermuda Registrar of Companies and the Bermuda Monetary Authority; the UK Prudential Regulation Authority has no direct supervisory mandate over Gibraltar-licensed banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The GIP is pegged at par to GBP, and both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible. Neither Gibraltar nor Bermuda maintains exchange-control permit regimes, capital import licensing, or profit-remittance restrictions. A Bermuda Exempted Company benefits from statutory exemption from Bermuda tax; dividends and capital repatriations to shareholders are free of Bermuda and Gibraltar withholding tax provided the company is not managed and controlled in Gibraltar. Treasury discipline requires that central management, board meetings, and strategic decision-making remain outside Gibraltar to preserve the tax-exempt and non-resident treasury status.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Neither Bermuda nor Gibraltar imposes statutory export-proceeds surrender timelines, mandatory conversion ratios, or repatriation windows. Receipts for ISIC 6201 payroll-software and automation services may be retained in GBP, USD, EUR, or other freely convertible currencies and settled according to commercial terms. Post-Brexit, EU capital-movement restrictions do not extend to Gibraltar, and no Bank of England or HM Treasury clearance is required for trade or service receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Operational Account (GBP) and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium feasibility. Global digital EMIs and fintech platforms (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Currenxie, Payoneer) generally decline a Bermuda Exempted Company presented as a Gibraltar external branch absent demonstrated substance, a licensed GFSC-regulated Gibraltar agent, and a compliance perimeter proving that client payroll funds never pass through the company balance sheet. The Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML classification and high payroll disbursement volumes trigger programme-level approval by the EMI's independent risk committee; acceptance is discretionary. A Gibraltar-licensed e-money institution, domiciled and regulated by the GFSC, is a more viable multicultural payment route when sponsored by a tier-1 domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: GFSC-compliant onboarding requires at least one director or ultimate beneficial owner to complete either an in-person interview at a Gibraltar branch or a supervised notarised video interview with live liveness verification and independent certification of identity by a Bermuda attorney, Gibraltar advocate, or notary. Fully non-face-to-face opening is exceptionally rare for an offshore Bermuda entity. The practical mandate is physical presence of the founder director at the chosen bank, or appointment of a Gibraltar resident director or GFSC-licensed nominee to appear, sign, and accept ongoing AML accountability for the external branch registered under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda Exempted Company flagged as an offshore tax-haven vehicle with non-public beneficial ownership and insufficient economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing from the Bermuda Registrar; Certificate of Incumbency; Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Register extract; notarised Memorandum of Association and Bye-laws; certified register of directors and shareholders; and a Bermuda legal opinion confirming exempt status, non-resident ownership, nil minimum capital requirement, and the absence of any bearer-share or no-liability features.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payroll automation commercial model misclassified as a money-services business or unlicensed payment institution due to aggregated payroll funds flowing through the company books.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited business plan and product data-flow diagrams showing pure software licensing and no client-money custody; executed SaaS and PaaS agreements confirming settlement is performed by FCA-approved or GFSC-approved payment institutions; ISO 27001 certificate and SOC 2 Type II report; and an independent AML/CTF risk assessment concluding the activity sits outside the E-Money Regulations 2011 and PSD2 licensing perimeter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source of wealth and source of funds for the opening capital injection from the overseas shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of personal or corporate bank statements of the remitting shareholder; sworn source-of-wealth declaration; capitalisation agreement; proof of incorporation expenses and independent valuation of capitalised intangible payroll software; and tax clearance certificates from the shareholder's residence jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanctions, or PEP screening hit against the founder or a nexus to a sanctioned jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clean Refinitiv World-Check or equivalent enhanced screening report dated within 30 days; statutory declaration of non-PEP status and absence of sanctions exposure; police clearance or equivalent good-conduct certification from the founder's country of residence; sanctions screening policy covering each payroll disbursement jurisdiction; and a documented negative-news research log evidencing reasonable investigation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unregistered status or absence of a licensed agent for the Bermuda company in Gibraltar, creating a regulatory-orphan profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar Companies House certificate of registration as an external company; appointment letter of a GFSC-licensed registered agent with statutory duty to maintain the Gibraltar beneficial ownership register; current Bermuda Certificate of Compliance; and a group structure chart showing the branch relationship and reporting lines.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity is routed by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the GIB GBP operational account with field 70 or 77B narrative 'EQUI - Direct Investment - Equity Capital Injection into Bermuda Exempted Company external branch, ISIC 6201 payroll SaaS'. No Gibraltar or Bermuda exchange-control approval, no Bank of England authorisation, and no capital-import certificate is required. The receiving bank will apply enhanced due diligence to the remitter and will request the board capitalisation resolution, the Gibraltar external branch registration certificate, and the Bermuda incorporation certificate. Denominate injections in GBP to eliminate GIP/GBP conversion cost (parity is fixed), and settle through GIB's UK correspondent using CHAPS for T+0/T+1 same-day value.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Global payroll settlements are executed as individual SWIFT MT103 messages or as ISO 20022 payment files aggregated into MT103 batches from the Gibraltar operational account through the bank's London correspondent. For high-value vendor and trade settlements, SWIFT MT202 COV cover payments and commercial letters of credit issued under UCP 600 and advised through the vendor's bank are the permissible clearing rails. SEPA direct debit and credit transfers are unavailable from Gibraltar (non-EEA post-Brexit). UK GBP payroll is cleared via CHAPS, BACS, or Faster Payments through the UK clearing bank partner; Direct Debit ACH collection of client payroll fees is implemented through an FCA-approved payment institution rather than the Gibraltar entity itself.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/GBP forward contracts executed with GIB treasury or a London dealing desk, with GIP/GBP parity eliminating any Gibraltar-pound conversion risk
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market payroll currencies (e.g., INR, PHP, BRL, MXN) transacted through GFSC-regulated banks or their London and Frankfurt execution desks
Cross-currency swaps (USD/GBP, USD/CHF, EUR/USD) for intra-group liquidity and balance-sheet hedging documented under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with prudentially licensed counterparties
Vanilla FX options and collars limited to budgeted payroll currency exposures within a rolling 12-month treasury hedge window and approved by the board's treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Annual Return (Form under Companies Act 2014 s.206/213)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 13 months of registration date at Gibraltar Companies Registry; every 13 months thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in monetary default penalties, loss of good standing, and administrative strike-off of the company from the Gibraltar Register under Companies Act 2014 s.379.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Exempted Company Annual Return (Companies Act 1981 s.124)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies (Corporate and Land Registry Services)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May for exempted companies (or within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation according to the Companies (Annual Returns) Regulations 2013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may trigger penalty fees under the Bermuda Companies (Annual Returns) Act, risk of strike-off and loss of exempted company status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar annual corporate income tax return (GSTF / Income Tax Act 2010)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office (Commissioner of Income Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 November following the fiscal year end (Gibraltar tax year: 1 July - 30 June); in some cases, filing due within 5 months of the company's accounting period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is subject to civil penalties of GIP 100 (flat penalty per year) plus interest; criminal liability up to GIP 10,000 and imprisonment for persistent non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Register of Beneficial Owners annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit / Companies Registry (Beneficial Ownership Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due within one month of the Register anniversary date; many private companies file by 31 January each year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance may lead to monetary penalties up to GIP 100,000 per breach and up to 2 years' imprisonment for officers under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2018.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar confirmation meeting / minutes of AGM (filed with annual return where required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records (Gibraltar Registrar of Companies registers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM held within 15 months of the previous AGM and within 9 months of the financial year end; annual return filed within 13 months of registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors are liable to a fine of GIP 25 per day for failure to hold AGM (Companies Act 2014 s.130); repeated defaults may result in strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit applies unless the company qualifies as a small company under Gibraltar Companies (Accounts) Act 2014 s.16: turnover below GIP 10.0 million, balance sheet total below GIP 5.0 million, and average employees below 50 (two of three criteria met). Companies that are public interest entities or members of an ineligible group are always audited.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by Gibraltar (mandatory for all companies preparing statutory accounts since 2016); UK GAAP (FRS 102) permitted under transitional concession for non-public-interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For each Register of Beneficial Owners year-end anniversary, Gibraltar resident officers must confirm change in Ultimate Beneficial Owners to GFIU/Companies Registry through the annual confirmation. Any transfer of shares in subsidiaries requires a UBO re-verification, and the beneficial-ownership confirmation must be made annually for each Gibraltar-incorporated vehicle, regardless of whether the underlying shareholders changed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of UBO/Registro de Beneficiarios Finales

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% flat rate for all commercial companies (Income Tax Act 2010, as amended); utilities and concession companies at higher hybrid rates; no surtax for payroll SaaS companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No tax holidays or patent box. Bermuda exemption certificate (Tax Exempted Status up to 2050) applies only to Bermuda tax and does not shield Gibraltar-resident managed operations. Gibraltar taxes worldwide income of companies managed and controlled in Gibraltar (s.11 ITA 2010). Incentives available: 100% first-year capital allowances on qualifying IP/software expenditure; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains on substantial shareholdings (≥5%); no capital gains tax except on real property; no VAT (0% GST) on software subscriptions; territorial exclusion for non-resident companies on foreign-source income unless remitted.
